summary: The verification finding rests on a count whose sources are broader than the set its target describes, and the question a reader will ask next is whether that is a one-off or a pattern, so I spent the last of the budget answering it rather than restating anything. Auditing every quorum-like count in the package against the set its target is computed over leaves one mismatch and four matches. The mismatch is the leader verification, which credits the leader with a vote before consulting any configuration and counts acknowledgements from every entry of its replication state, non-voting members included, while its target counts voters only. The matches are the election, which asks only voters for votes and tallies only those replies; the pre-vote, which also asks voters only; the commitment calculation, whose match map is built and rebuilt from voter entries alone so other members' acknowledgements cannot enter it; and the leader lease, which records a contact only for servers whose suffrage is voter. Commit, election, pre-vote and lease therefore each compare a voter-derived count against a voter-derived target, and the verification is the single place where the two sets diverge. I recorded that as one behaviour citing all six sites plus the commitment construction, so the boundary of the finding is explicit and a later reader does not have to re-audit four other paths to know it, and I noted that the audit covers the counts used for those decisions rather than every message tally in the package. No execution was spent, since the four matches and the one mismatch are all visible in code already cited. That is where the run's budget ends: the record holds the witnessed behaviours with their receipts and controls, the source-decided gate bypass and verification findings with their scopes, the conditional account of the regression under application order at the shared store key, and the several scoped negatives - the log cache, the commit index arithmetic, and the bootstrap term write - each with the boundary that keeps it honest.
